tasks.short: Collaborate on menus and serving arrangements

steps.what: Gather current menu, recipe cost and serving constraints before the meeting
Conduct meetings and agree menu and serving arrangements with other personnel
Write the agreed menu and serving details into the working service plan
Check and circulate the final service plan to the participating teams

tasks.design: Use native menu and cost views in {OPS_SYSTEM} and the existing service-plan layout in {DOCS}. The supervisor collaborates personally, writes the actual agreed details and checks the exact version circulated through {EMAIL}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Preparing references and rebuilding stable service-plan sections add clerical work around meetings.
tasks.enabler_now: Native recipe views and reusable plan sections make existing information easier to use.
tasks.still_hard: Menu choices and serving trade-offs need agreement between people.
tasks.human_edge: The supervisor reconciles kitchen capacity and service needs.
tasks.altitude: Reduce preparation and plan transcription while retaining collaboration.

reach.learn: Which serving arrangements constrain kitchen choices

evidence.claim: Apicbase supports recipe costing from ingredient prices; this supports reference availability, not automated meetings or agreement.
Reference and plan-writing savings are unmeasured estimates.

assumptions: The existing working service plan is the artefact used by kitchen and serving teams. Its actual writing and send are included separately from the meeting; no additional minutes or trailing conversation record is invented.

The chef produces menu and recipe references, purchasing maintains ingredient prices and the supervisor gathers serving constraints in s1. The meeting produces decisions in s2 and the supervisor captures them in s3. Missing or stale references require manual checking within retained work.

Native context views remove three of15 reference hours. Reusable stable plan sections remove7.5 of25 repeated-context/formatting hours, leaving17.5 for actual decisions, checks and ordinary same-system saves without self-approval.
No model summary, automatic publication or task assignment is implied. All colleague discussion uses internal authority.
unknowns: How much of the present service plan is genuinely reusable
research_questions: Which plan sections can be reused without concealing changed serving decisions?

already_counted.description: Reference checking and actual plan writing remain in s1 and s3.

incremental.description: Supervisor updates the plan layout after service-format changes.

approvals.approved_version: Exact dated menu, serving arrangements, responsibilities and receiving teams checked before circulation; edits invalidate the check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: E1 B100 R89.5, gross10.5 less upkeep1 gives net9.5. Low0 retains the existing process where references and plan sections are already reused and no configuration is adopted. High6 retains14 reference hours and19 plan-writing hours because some cost references and service sections need manual reconstruction, plus60 meeting/send hours: R93, net6. Central retains12 reference and17.5 plan hours with compatible layouts.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Develop maintenance schedules and arrange repairs

steps.what: Gather equipment identifiers, maintenance guidance, last service dates and reported faults
Choose maintenance timing and the urgency and scope of repairs
Write the equipment maintenance schedule with the chosen dates and access windows
Draft the repair request with equipment, fault and access details
Check and send the final repair request to the service contractor
Agree repair attendance and coordinate practical access with the contractor

tasks.design: Use equipment-linked reference views in {PROJECT} and {DOCS}, reusable maintenance-schedule rows and an existing repair-request layout. The supervisor chooses dates and scope, writes actual changes, checks the request sent through {EMAIL} and agrees access personally.
tasks.previous_blocker: Equipment references, repeated schedule rows and standard repair context are copied across documents and messages.
tasks.enabler_now: Native project views and reusable fields can remove those specific clerical operations.
tasks.still_hard: Fault urgency, safe access and service disruption need operational judgement.
tasks.human_edge: The supervisor balances equipment risk against practical service continuity.
tasks.altitude: Prepare maintenance arrangements with less repeated equipment-context writing.

reach.learn: Which fault descriptions enable useful repair preparation

evidence.claim: Equipment-linked references and reusable schedule/request fields are a plausible native configuration; the digest supplies no measured maintenance-administration case.

assumptions: The maintenance schedule and contractor request are existing working artefacts. The task includes writing, actual sending and access discussion but adds no new completion or fault log.

Equipment administration produces identifiers, the manufacturer supplies maintenance guidance and prior service staff produce service dates in existing records. The supervisor gathers and validates these in s1 and captures observed fault scope and chosen timing in s2/s4. Missing service history is manually investigated; there is no free due-for-service flag.

Native equipment views remove three of15 retrieval hours. Reused schedule rows remove10 of25 stable-row entry hours; request fields remove4.5 of15 equipment/context copying hours. Actual scheduling judgement, fault description, checking and same-system saves remain.
No recurrence engine, automatic reminder, supplier booking or maintenance alert is implied; every actual send or agreement remains in s5/s6.
unknowns: Whether current schedules already reuse recurring rows
research_questions: Which request fields can be reused without obscuring the actual fault or current access conditions?

already_counted.description: Equipment reference checks and actual schedule/request writing remain in s1, s3 and s4.

incremental.description: Supervisor updates reference links and request defaults after equipment changes.

approvals.approved_version: Exact equipment identifier, reported fault, requested scope, access windows and contractor recipient checked before sending; changes invalidate the check.
Actual attendance/access agreement and service scope checked against current operating constraints before communicating agreement; changed terms require a renewed check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: E1 B100 R82.5, gross17.5 less upkeep1.5 gives net16. Low3 retains all15 retrieval hours,22 schedule hours and13.5 request hours because equipment history is incomplete and most arrangements differ, plus45 judgement/send/discussion hours: R95.5, net3. High11 retains13 retrieval,18 schedule and11.5 request hours for partly reusable equipment context, plus45 other hours: R87.5, net11. Central retains12,15 and10.5 clerical hours respectively; no flat cut determines these operations.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Retain menu collaboration and maintenance judgement while reducing repeated planning documents and equipment context.
reach: Chefs aligning menus with service arrangements
Technicians preparing for clearly described repairs
role.ambitious_version: A food service supervisor who keeps shared plans and repair arrangements clear without rebuilding standard context each time.

job.title: First-Line Supervisors of Food Preparation and Serving Workers
